segments.title: The footprint that said buy, and delta
sections: Delta, Cumulative Delta And The Footprint

cues.text: You know the bar. Price drops into the prior-day low, the footprint lights up with selling, and a fat negative number looks finished. You buy.
The next bar prints the same number and keeps going. Twenty minutes later, mid-range, a stack of buying imbalances. You buy that too.
Neither trade was a read. Both were a number taken as an order. The footprint has a signal on every bar if you want one.
This module reads it at a level, a price marked before the session, as confirmation only, every setting written down.
Every contract that trades has two sides: a resting limit order, and someone crossing the spread to hit it. The one who crosses is the aggressor.
Price moves when aggressors use up the resting orders at one price and reach for the next. What differs is who was in a hurry.
The footprint chart shows the volume at each price inside each bar, split into buying at the ask and selling at the bid. Delta is the difference.
A 1-minute MNQ bar with 820 contracts at the ask and 690 at the bid has a bar delta of plus 130.
Passive orders never appear in delta, so price can rise on a bar with negative delta: the bids held and the offers above were pulled.
Delta tells you who pushed. Price tells you whether the push worked.
Cumulative delta is the running total of bar delta since the open. It is slow, it can stay positive through a fall, and it is context, never a signal.
It is the most comforting number on the screen, because it changes slowly. Comfort is not a read.
One setting decides every number. NinjaTrader 8 classifies trades in BidAsk or UpDownTick mode, and the two do not give the same numbers.
The rule: read per-bar delta at the level, treat cumulative delta as context only, and write the delta mode on every screenshot you save.
Getting it wrong is a rising cumulative delta line read as buyers in control, and a long taken mid-range. It reveals a wish for one number to hand you the direction.
The fix: cumulative delta lives in a panel below the chart, never on the price pane and never in a branch, an if-then line of your plan.
Every saved screenshot carries a label with three items.
One: the timeframe.
Two: the delta mode.
Three: live or reloaded.

segments.title: Imbalances, your settings, and absorption
sections: Imbalances, Stacks And Your Own Settings

cues.text: A footprint is read diagonally: buying at a price against selling one tick below it, because buyers lift the offer, one tick above the bid.
Past a ratio and a minimum difference you set, the cell is flagged: a diagonal imbalance. Not the auction imbalance of Module 5.
Four rows of one bar, ratio 5, minimum 15.
One: 96 against 14, nearly 7 to 1. Flagged.
Two: 88 against 16. Flagged.
Three: 71 against 9. Flagged.
Four: 20 against 6, about 3 to 1. Not flagged.
Three flagged cells on adjacent prices, same side: a stacked imbalance. On the 5-minute footprint, a location, never a trigger.
The platform default, ratio 1.5 and minimum delta 10, flags almost every bar. A chart that is always shouting has nothing to say.
This course starts at ratio 5, minimum delta 15: a working default, a setting you start from because you need one, chosen for screen clarity.

You cannot backtest one ratio against another across years; stamped tick data does not go back far enough. In replay you can count stacks at a level against stacks mid-range: occurrences, not an edge.
The rule: your settings are written down, saved as one chart template, and changed only at a scheduled review, as a dated line.
Getting it wrong is the ratio dropped to 3 at 10:20 because nothing was flagging. It reveals a chart tuned until it shows the trade you want.
The fix: one template named with its settings, FP 5-15 BidAsk, and a dated change log. Changes take effect the next session.
Now, absorption. Price falls into the prior-day low zone, the band around a level. Bar after bar prints minus 200 and worse. Price does not go lower.
Resting bids are filling every seller. It lasts only while price holds. Trade through and build time beyond, and that is acceptance: the read flips.
The rule: absorption counts only at a named level, while price holds the zone, and with a price event after it. A 1-minute close beyond the far edge, the edge away from price, ends it.
Getting it wrong is a long on the third minus 200 bar, mid-range, in a down session. It reveals the most dramatic picture taken as an answer. The next bars settle it.
The fix: the plan line names the end of the read, a 1-minute close beyond the far edge price. No number to type, no read. Only a big number.

segments.title: Trapped traders and the four failures

cues.text: A failed breakdown has a recognisable footprint. Price breaks below a level, and the breaking bar stacks selling imbalances near its low: traders selling the break.
Two 1-minute bars close below. Then a 1-minute bar closes back above, and delta flips positive. The sellers of the low are trapped: short below price, stops above.
The signature has three parts.
One: stacked imbalances at the extreme.
Two: after two 1-minute closes beyond the level, a 1-minute close back through it.
Three: delta flipping to the other side.
Read the failure, not the story about who has to cover.
The rule: write trapped only when all three parts are on the chart at a named level, and act only after the reclaim and a trigger, the price event that puts you in.
Getting it wrong is a long into the sweep bar itself because everyone below is trapped. The story feels certain. Price has not read it.
It reveals a trade on other people’s pain. The fix: three boxes on the plan line. No order with a box empty.
Now, the four failures. The useful question at a level is narrow: is the side pushing into it running out? One confirmation field records that, in four sub-forms.
For a long at a level below price. One: big-orders. Passive size holds and prints at the level, 180, then 210, then 150, and no bar trades below it.
Two: failing-delta. Each approach bar carries less selling than the one before: minus 158, minus 92, minus 37.
Three: delta-divergence. Price makes a new low on approach and delta does not: minus 240 on the earlier push, minus 60 on the lower low.
Four: two-bar-exhaustion. A bar with deep opposing delta closes near its extreme in the direction of your read, then the next bar breaks it.
Approach, not arrival, matters for the delta reads. The approach is the run of bars toward the zone, up to the first touch.
Inside the zone the resting orders answer, and delta describes the reaction you are about to see in price anyway. After arrival, a divergence is the reaction, not a warning.
The rule: record exactly which sub-form you saw, before entry. Failing-delta and delta-divergence are read from approach bars only.

Getting it wrong is a confirmation field that says order flow on forty trades. It reveals a record that cannot separate four events. The fix: a drop-down with five values, the four sub-forms and none.

options: A stack of imbalances at the extreme
Cumulative delta turning positive for the session
Two 1-minute closes beyond, then a close back through
Delta flipping to the other side
check.why: The three parts are the stack, the closes and the reclaim, and the bar delta flip. Cumulative delta is session context.

options: A read of the failure itself
A trade on the story of other people’s pain, before price has said anything
check.why: The story feels certain before price has said anything. The order waits for the reclaim and a trigger.

check.q: Three approach bars print −158, −92 and −37 while price keeps falling into your zone. Which sub-form?
check.why: Each bar into the level carries less selling than the one before: failing-delta, complete before arrival.

check.q: A delta divergence shows up only after price is inside the zone. How is it recorded?
options: It is not recorded: after arrival it is the reaction, not a warning
check.why: Delta-divergence and failing-delta are read from approach bars only. Inside the zone, delta describes the reaction.

sections: Early Reads, And Reading What You Want

cues.text: Every trade in this course follows one chain: idea, then setup, a location and a read together, then trigger, then construction. Order flow sits beside the trigger, never in its place.
A confirmed entry has two parts: a recorded sub-form, and a price event, a bar close or a break of structure.
The failing delta tells you the selling is drying up. Only a close tells you buyers have done something about it.
Footprint events are quick and often reversed within a bar. A close is fixed once it prints. That is why the order waits for the close.
The rule: no order is placed on a footprint number. A trade that uses order flow needs a recorded sub-form and a Module 13 trigger fired at the level.
Getting it wrong is a buy stop one tick above an exhaustion print, filled before the bar closed. It reveals trust in the faster, noisier, more easily reversed of the two.
The fix: the ticket is not armed until the trigger bar has closed. The plan line carries the condition, a 1-minute close above a price.
The first fifteen to twenty minutes after the 9:30 a.m. open are price discovery. Overnight orders hit from both sides, and bar delta flips sign bar to bar.
Big deltas print everywhere. The footprint is having a wonderful time. It is not an invitation.
There is no clock ban on the opening minutes. There is arithmetic: wider early structure, a wider stop behind the far edge, smaller size.
The session block, early, mid or late, is recorded on every trade, so your record can compare your early reads with your later ones.
The harder part is you. A mind that wants a trade finds one on the footprint, and that is how trades happen mid-range, where nothing sits under the stop.
The rule: the footprint is read only for a named zone, the approach bars into it and the bars inside it, up to the trigger. Same read in the opening block, with size from the wider stop.
Getting it wrong is a string of mid-range trades in the first twenty minutes, each on a footprint number that looked like the setup. It reveals a footprint asked to find the trade for you.
The fix: keep the footprint panel closed. Each zone carries a near-edge and a far-edge alert. The footprint opens when the near-edge alert fires, and closes when price leaves without a trigger.

check.q: What are the two parts of a confirmed entry?
options: A sub-form and a cumulative delta reading
A recorded sub-form and a price event: a close or a structure break
A footprint print and a stop
check.why: Order flow confirms; only a price event triggers. Both are needed, and the ticket is armed on the close.

check.q: A buy stop sits one tick above an exhaustion print and fills before the bar closes. What does it reveal?
options: Trust in the faster, noisier, more easily reversed of the two
Nothing, if the level was right
check.why: The footprint moves faster than price and is often reversed within the bar. The order waits for the close.

check.q: In the first twenty minutes, what does wider structure change?
options: The clock: no trades until 9:50 a.m.
The read: the footprint is ignored
The stop is wider, so size is smaller
check.why: There is no clock ban. Wider early structure means a wider stop behind the far edge and smaller size.

check.q: When does the footprint panel open?
options: At 9:30 a.m., and it stays open
When a near-edge alert fires on a marked zone
check.why: The panel stays closed until price reaches a zone, so the footprint cannot go looking for a trade mid-range.

cues.text: A hypothetical illustration, not a trade record: a composite MNQ footprint, invented prices. It stops at the trigger: no entry, no outcome.
The plan, written at 9:25 a.m.: accept above the pd-high zone, the prior-day high, 21,684 to 21,690; then a Pause N Go, the Module 13 trigger, on the first pullback; target 21,790.
Invalidation, the price that proves it wrong: a 5-minute close below 21,684. Confirmation is not on the line; you record it if it shows.
At 10:05 a 5-minute bar closes at 21,712, above the zone: acceptance. The footprint stays closed.
At 10:17 price pulls back to 21,690; the near-edge alert fires and the footprint opens. Read the approach bars back.
10:14, delta minus 158. Approach, sellers pushing.
10:15, a lower low, minus 92. Less selling.
10:16, minus 37. Third weaker bar: failing-delta, complete before the zone.
10:17, minus 12. Arrival, the first touch.
10:18 and 10:19, plus 6 and plus 11. Two bars inside the zone, no close below 21,684: the pause of Pause N Go.
The arrival bars turned positive and asked to join the read. They are the reaction. A warning that arrives with the thing it warns about is a caption.
Not there: no earlier push to diverge from, no bid holding size, no deep bar closing high. One sub-form, by name.
The trigger still has to print: Pause N Go’s second half, a 1-minute close above the pause high, 21,690. Until then the delta is an observation; the ticket is not armed.
A close below 21,684 means no trigger. If it fires, the stop goes behind the far edge; size is Module 14. The case stops here.
Now, your score. Your last ten trades with the footprint open before entry. One point per line.
One: location. Inside a named zone, not mid-range.
Two: trigger. A price event, not a footprint number.
Three: sub-form. The field names exactly one, or none.
Four: approach. Failing-delta or delta-divergence complete before the first touch.
Five: settings. Your written template, unchanged, mode on the screenshot.
Lines 1 and 2 override. Two or more of ten missing either: fix those first. Footprint closed outside a zone, no order before the close.
If none do, find the line from 3 to 5 most missed. Three or more, and it goes on your pre-market sheet.
Getting it wrong is scoring from memory. It reveals a record kept in your head. Score from the journal.

cues.text: Before your next session, one line. Before any entry on a trade where you looked at the footprint, write in the trade note the sub-form name, then the price event you are waiting for.
Like this: failing-delta; 1-minute close above 21,690. That is the whole assignment.
The rule: the line is written before the entry, never after. A number on a footprint is not an order. It is not even a suggestion. It is a number.
Getting it wrong is the line written after the fill, from memory. It reveals a note kept to look like a process. The fix: no line, no entry, and the note shows its time.
In one line: order flow tells you whether the side pushing into your level is running out; only a price event tells you it has.
Where it goes next. Module 8, The Three Tiers, places this confirmation in the chain, beside the trigger and never in its tier.
Module 6 carries the stacked imbalance as an in-session location, built with the settings you wrote down here.
Module 13 defines the price events every confirmed trade still needs, Pause N Go first. Module 11 is where trapped traders confirm a failed breakdown read.
In the journal, Module 18, the confirmation field and the session block are recorded on every trade, so your review can sort by them.
For why footprint reads are hard to test across years, and what you can count instead, Module 22.
The settings and delta modes on this page come from NinjaTrader’s own help guide for Order Flow Volumetric Bars, linked on the page.
